brief: The ground cache is the frame's biggest single cost and the camera makes it worse. c258 merges three cues: `drawGround` costs 25-27 ms; it rebuilds about 2.5 times more per sim day than it did at #138; an ease repaints the destination on the frame it STOPS, so the distance visibly crisps at u=1; and a follow holds the wide cache at 54% detail for the whole move. Cut the rebuild rate and make the ease land without the snap, so that moving the camera — the loop's newest and most-used interaction — costs less and does not announce its own arrival. Why now: three cues merged into one, and #166's follow made the cache the thing the observer touches most.
successLooksLike: `probes/ground-rebuilds.mjs` and `probes/ground-cost.mjs` quote rebuilds per sim day and ms per rebuild before and after, both improved; a filmstrip across an ease shows no single-frame crisp at the end of the move; the wide frame is byte-identical at rest.
avoid: ANYTHING THAT MOVES THE FRAME must hold the padded WIDE ground cache for the whole move and repaint ONCE on release — do not solve the crisp by repainting during the ease. LAWS: the ground is a CACHE, so a per-frame truth on it is a live overlay, and anything registered in SCREEN space at cache time (FACES) goes stale through the ease and must be mapped through k = viewS/gview.s. Do not touch what is DRAWN; this brief changes when and at what detail, not what.
